Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILGNAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph OPINION NO. 07 AUG 2019 s. 202 HON. ROWENA S. AFRICA Office of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Province of Batangas Dear Hon. Africa: This is in reference to your letter dated 19 February 2019 seeking clarification on the following inquiries, viz: 1. Is it possible for the SK Chairpersons and SK Kagawad to avail Special Program Por Employment of Students (SPES) here in the Province of Batangas? 2. Is it possible to waive honorarium of SK Chairpersons in their barangay then accept the Job Order position in the Province of Batangas? Since your issues are interrelated, we deemed it prudent to answer the same in one discussion only. Your queries basically cover "employment" and hiring of SK Chairperson as Job Orders in the Province of Batangas. Foremost, we would like to remind you of the prohibition provided in Section 94(a) of Republic Act 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, which states: "No elective or appointive official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity_ to_ any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no elective or appointive local official shall hold any other office or employment in the Government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries. "

Moreover, this Department, in DILG Opinion No. 66 s. 2018, already settled the issue on hiring of SK Officials as Job Orders in this wise: "In view of the foregoing, it is our opinion that the law intended the public officials not to hold any position in the government in whatever capacity, unless specifically allowed by law. On the other hand, even if it was established that JO and COS has no employer-employee (EE-ER) relationship with the government, being a JO or COS in the government is still an "employment in the government" or he is considered "holding a public Therefore, we find the herein principle office". applicable, viz: "What cannot be legally done directly cannot be done indirectly. This rule is basic and, to a reasonable mind, does not need explanation. Indeed, if acts that cannot be legally done directly can be done indirectly, then all laws would be illusory.l" In other words, since elective officials are proscribed to be employed in the government during their tenure, they should not be allowed to circumvent the law by hiring them in the guise of JO or COS, because it will make this proscription useless, and will result in doing indirectly what is not legal. Hence, it is this Department's position that elective or appointive local officials cannot be hired as JO or COS employee in any government office or GOCC. Lastly, please be informed however, that SK Officials are allowed to accept employment in private offices or practice their profession as long as it does not conflict with his/her duties in the SK. " TAWANG MULTI-PURPOSE COOPERATIVE vs.LA TRINIDAD WATER DISTRICT, G.R. No. 166471, March 22, 2011

In view of the foregoing, this Department answers both your queries in negative. We hope we have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARIVEL C. SA ENDONCILLO, CESO 111 ndersecretary LIIs/37
